The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[17–20] ﴿Do they not look at the camels, how they were created?﴾ ﴿And at the sky, how it was raised?﴾ [Al-Ghashiyah: 18] ﴿And at the mountains, how they were set up?﴾ [Al-Ghashiyah: 19] ﴿And at the earth, how it was spread out?﴾ [Al-Ghashiyah: 20]

(p-6140) ﴿Do they not look at the camels, how they were created?﴾ Abu al-Su'ud said: It is a resumptive clause (isti'naf) brought to illustrate what has been detailed of the narrative of the Overwhelming Event and what it rests upon, namely the Resurrection about which they dispute, by way of offering as evidence what they cannot deny. The hamzah is for rebuke and reproach, and the fa' is for coordination with an implied antecedent that the context requires. The word "kayfa" (how) is in the accusative, governed by what follows it, and it suspends the verb of seeing (nazar). The clause lies in the position of a genitive, as a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimal) for "al-ibil" (the camels). That is: do they deny what has been mentioned of the Resurrection and its rulings, and deem its occurrence far-fetched from the power of God, Mighty and Majestic, so that they do not look at the camels, which are before their eyes and which they use at all times, to see how they were created, a wondrous creation, distinguished from the customary forms of the creation of the rest of the species of animals, in the massiveness of their bodies, the strength of their power, and the wondrous shape suited to their performing the arduous tasks that proceed from them, such as rising with heavy loads and dragging grievous burdens to distant regions, and in their patience over hunger and thirst, to the extent that their thirst may reach ten days or more, and their contentment with little, and their grazing on whatever is available of thorns, trees and other things that scarcely any other beast would graze upon, and in their submission, despite all this, to man in movement and rest, kneeling and rising, for he uses them in that as he wills, and every young and old person leads them.

﴿And at the sky﴾ [Al-Ghashiyah: 18], which they witness every moment by night and by day, ﴿how it was raised﴾ [Al-Ghashiyah: 18], that is: its stars were raised to a far-reaching height, and each of them was held in its orbit with a holding that does not disturb its course nor corrupt its order.

﴿And at the mountains﴾ [Al-Ghashiyah: 19], that is, those in whose regions they dwell, ﴿how they were set up﴾ [Al-Ghashiyah: 19], that is: they were fixed erect, never leaving their place, as a safeguard for the earth against shaking.

﴿And at the earth﴾ [Al-Ghashiyah: 20], that is, the one upon which they travel and move about, ﴿how it was spread out﴾ [Al-Ghashiyah: 20], that is: it was extended and made a level bed, according to what the welfare of the affairs of the creatures upon it requires.

Al-Zamakhshari said: The meaning is: Do they not look at these created things, which bear witness to the power of the Creator, so that they do not deny His capacity to resurrect, and so that they hear the warning of the Messenger (ﷺ), believe in it, and prepare for meeting Him?

A Subtlety:

Al-Sakkaki mentioned in (al-Miftah), in the discussion of the imaginative faculty (al-jami' al-khayali), that its gathering follows the course of habit and custom (p-6141) according to what the causes establish in depositing images in the storehouse of imagination. And that if one does not give it its due of alertness, and he is of the people of the settled towns (madar), how can the speech of the Lord of Might be sweet to the people of the tents (wabar), since it makes them see the proofs arranged in that order: "Do they not look at the camels, how they were created," and the rest of the verses, because the camel is distant from their imagination at the point of looking, then because it is distant in their imagination from the sky, and the distance of its creation from its being raised, and likewise the rest. **On the interpretation of His saying (Exalted is He):**

[21–26] ﴿So remind, for you are only a reminder﴾ ﴿You are not over them a controller﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 22] ﴿except for one who turns away and disbelieves﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 23] ﴿then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 24] ﴿Indeed, to Us is their return﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 25] ﴿then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 26]

﴿So remind﴾, meaning: those to whom you have been sent, with His signs, Exalted is He, which the natural disposition (fitrah) leads to belief in their Creator. ﴿for you are only a reminder﴾, meaning: a conveyor of what has been forgotten of His command, Exalted is He.

﴿You are not over them a controller﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 22], meaning: you are not one who holds power over them, compelling them to believe. It was also recited with the *sad* (ص) in place of the *sin* (س) in *muṣayṭir* (مُصَيْطِرٍ), by substituting it for the sin.

﴿except for one who turns away and disbelieves﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 23] ﴿then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 24], which is the punishment of Hell. The exception is disjunctive (munqati', an exception not belonging to the same category as what precedes it), meaning: "but whoever turns away and disbelieves, indeed power and dominion belong to Allah, so He will punish him with the greatest punishment for his denial of the truth."

﴿Indeed, to Us is their return﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 25], meaning: their return and their resurrection, through death and resurrection. This clause gives the reason for His punishing him with the greatest punishment. The pronoun in it and in what follows is plural, in consideration of the meaning of "man" (مَن), just as its singular form before it is in consideration of its wording.

﴿then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 26], meaning: We will requite them with the greatest punishment, for power and domination belong to Him alone, Exalted is He.

The exception is disjunctive (munqati', an exception not belonging to the same category as what precedes it), meaning: "but whoever turns away and disbelieves, indeed power and dominion belong to Allah, so He will punish him with the greatest punishment for his denial of the truth."

﴿Indeed, to Us is their return﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 25], meaning: their return and their resurrection, through death and resurrection. This clause gives the reason for His punishing him with the greatest punishment. The pronoun in it and in what follows is plural, in consideration of the meaning of "man" (مَن), just as its singular form before it is in consideration of its wording.

﴿then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 26], meaning: We will requite them with the greatest punishment, for power and domination belong to Him alone, Exalted is He.
